blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: The page lists the ways ISO 20022 differs from ISO-8583. Which of these is NOT one of its points?

options.text: It allows more flexible message structures and easier new fields
options.says: The page makes this point: flexibility is the second difference it lists.

options.text: It aims to standardize messages beyond payments, across financial domains
options.says: The page makes this point: standardization across domains is the third difference it lists.

options.text: It replaces the bitmap with named elements that describe themselves
options.says: The page never mentions bitmaps in its comparison; its five points are the data model, flexibility, standardization, rich metadata and an XML basis.

options.text: It carries richer metadata on the purpose and context of a transaction
options.says: The page makes this point: rich metadata is the fourth difference it lists.

questions.stem: While both standards coexist, the page's DualFormatGateway takes messages of either kind. How does it decide which kind of processing a message gets?

options.text: By reading the MTI, and treating a message without one as ISO 20022
options.says: The gateway never reads an MTI; it checks whether the message is an ISOMsg or a Document.

options.text: By looking at the first byte for an XML opening angle bracket
options.says: The gateway inspects no bytes; it receives objects and checks whether each is an ISOMsg or a Document.

options.text: By translating every message to ISO 20022 before processing it
options.says: The gateway processes an ISOMsg as ISO-8583 and translates only when convertToISO20022 is called.

options.text: By whether it is an ISOMsg or a Document, refusing anything else
options.says: processMessage branches on instanceof ISOMsg and instanceof Document, and throws IllegalArgumentException for any other format.
